title: Can Facebook Ads Prevent Malaria? Two Field Experiments in India
authors: Dante Donati; Nandan Rao; Victor Orozco-Olvera; Ana Maria Munoz Boudet
eligible_reason: Cluster-randomized field experiments with a single campaign start. Survey outcomes (Tables 6-10, 12-13) are treatment-vs-control regressions with state (strata) FE, OLS and logit. The administrative HMIS incidence analysis (Table 11, Figure 5, Tables D10-D17) is a randomized DiD: treatment_post = treatment x post with post = date_numeric>=22159 (September 2020) for every subdistrict, absorb(subdistrict_id month year) plus state_id#post and post-interacted cluster/subdistrict controls in columns 2-3, 5-6, 8-9. One common post date, so not a staggered adoption design.
design_notes: Stata. 00_Masterfile.do runs cleaning (01-07_Clean_*.do) and Table/Figure do-files. Table11_incidence_dd.do: reghdfe incidence_rate/uincidence_rate/rincidence_rate treatment_post con timeFE [controls_post] state_id#post if share_pop>0.5, absorb(subdistrict_id month year) cluster(district_id). TableD17 adds Poisson count versions.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). RCT with a common post date; no staggered adoption.
